# Apply Fixes

## Change Summary

No additional fixes were applied in this Apply Fixes stage. The latest review approved the producer-loss clamping, nitrifier source-pool bookkeeping, periphyton overflow routing, and budget-helper documentation amendments without follow-up changes, so the code remains as produced in the most recent implement stage.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Reviewed the latest validation output and confirmed the fifth review approved the implementation with no required amendments.
2. [Completed] Verified that no additional code edits were necessary for the producer-loss routing fixes, nitrifier bookkeeping changes, or canonical budget-helper documentation/tests.
3. [Skipped] Rerun validation after applying fixes.

## Validation Evidence

- Review outcome was `approved` with no follow-up amendments or blocking findings.
- No new validation commands were required in this stage because no code changed; prior validation remains authoritative.
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test budget_tracking` previously passed (17 tests).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test cycling` previously passed (12 tests).
- `cargo test -p tank_core` previously passed across the full `tank_core` suite, and `cargo clippy -p tank_core -- -D warnings` previously passed.

## Outstanding Risks

- The structural canonical-helper coverage guard remains convention-based rather than reflective; future explicit N/C-bearing fields with non-standard names or fields hidden in empty-by-default collections will require extending the discovery rules and tests.
- Shrimp eggs are still implicit until hatch; mass is conserved by debiting dissolved pools on hatch and maturation, but a future phase may still want an explicit egg or clutch biomass pool for clearer persistence and tracing.
- Complex multi-process stages such as `system:nitrogen_cycle` still rely on snapshot-derived gross component budgets, so same-component turnover inside a single pass can remain collapsed until those stages emit fully explicit source/sink deltas.
